lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi María, it's Kendra from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Kendra. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your body feeling this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not great. I've been really tired.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to be in bed by 10:30 on 4 nights. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It didn't happen this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your phone in the bedroom at night?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. My mom is staying with us and I'm taking care of her.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've been taking care of everybody.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Keeping the phone out of the bedroom helps a lot of people fall asleep faster.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Between appointments and everything, there was no time. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The days got away from you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Between appointments and everything, there was no time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you watch TV in bed?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Work has been crazy, I'm doing overtime.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have more energy when I go to bed earlier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the bedtime goal fit in your day?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've always eaten late, that's how we do it at home.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've tried before and it didn't stick.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the bedtime goal. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to be in bed by 10:30 on 5 nights.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 5.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 5 and not a 2?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 0 out of 4 days, the hard part was work, and next week you're going to be in bed by 10:30 on 5 nights. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Oh, before you go, i get out of breath just walking to the kitchen.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Thank you for telling me. That's something your care team needs to hear today. I'm going to call the nurse line as soon as we hang up, and if it gets worse, please go to the ER or call 911.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, thank you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, María. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Explores what would make it easier
States ability to manage three days
Trait claim conflicts with 0 of 4 days
Recognizes energy benefit of earlier bed
Asks where goal fits in day
Plans night before, believes it works
Asks what is doable next week
Reason: feels better when sticking to it
Breathless walking to kitchen; needs same-day care
Plans nurse call; delayed, no severity check
Sets midweek text and next contact

flags.reason: Participant reports breathlessness walking short distances; coach deferred nurse call until after hang-up and did not ask about rest symptoms, chest pain, or current severity before moving on.
'Once you decide something, you follow through' contradicts participant's 0 of 4 days; pressures rather than evokes.
Coach reframed goal as 'getting your life back' right after participant voiced ambivalence about timing; may push agenda rather than elicit participant's meaning.
After 'I've always eaten late...' and 'after the summer' sustain talk, coach moved on without exploring ambivalence.

score.summary: The coach used good open questions, autonomy-supporting language, and a clear summary to build a specific five-night bedtime goal with confidence ratings. However, the participant's breathlessness on exertion was only partially addressed: the nurse call was deferred until after hang-up with no check on current symptoms or severity.
strengths: Line 16: asked permission before sharing the phone-out-of-bedroom idea.
Line 42 and 45: emphasized autonomy with 'It's your plan' and 'completely your call.'
Line 48: 'Why a 5 and not a 2?' drew out the participant's own reasons for confidence.
Line 50: accurate summary of barriers and new goal before closing.
coaching_tips: Line 52: when a participant reports breathlessness, ask immediately whether it is at rest, with chest pain, or worsening, and escalate before moving on.
Line 28: avoid trait claims like 'you follow through' that the participant's own data contradicts; reflect what she did instead.
Line 36: when sustain talk ('after the summer', 'I've always eaten late') appears, explore ambivalence with a complex reflection before setting goals.
Line 13 and 25: name caregiving and overtime barriers with a complex reflection, then ask what would help, rather than moving straight to goal setting.
